questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down above a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put your vehicle in "park" when parking on a hill. Turn your front wheels away from the center of the road if there is no curb. If there is a curb, point your wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may slip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, what should you do?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.
Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with multiple vehicles arriving at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers then go in the order they arrived.

questions.question: What should you do as you approach the top of a hill?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle may be stopped just out of sight. Always slow down enough to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign but no painted crosswalk, where must you stop?

options.text: Stop your vehicle inside the unmarked crosswalk.
Stop before entering the unmarked crosswalk.
Stop at the stop sign. It does not matter if you are in the crosswalk or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the crosswalk. The crosswalk may be marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey them?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create extra space ahead and slow down gradually. Do not brake suddenly. You can also move to another lane if safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling that they will turn right. Watch for this signal and adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Change in direction ahead.
School zone and crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a two-way road.

questions.question: A yellow light that flashes on and off means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: Fines for speeding are tripled in work and school zones.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Fines for speeding are doubled (not tripled) in work zones when workers are present and in school zones during school hours. Always drive slowly and carefully near workers and children.

questions.question: When making an emergency roadside stop, you should:

options.text: Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Put the car in park and set the parking brake.
Leave your vehicle running and exit the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the car in park and set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop on the side of the road, signal and pull as far off the road as you can. Put the car in park, set the parking brake, turn on emergency flashers, turn off the engine, and remove the keys. Check traffic before you get out.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe following distance between vehicles?

options.text: Three seconds.
Five seconds.
Seven seconds.

questions.explanation: You should stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: When should you enter a roundabout?

options.text: Only when there is a safe gap in traffic.
Right away, because entering traffic always has the right-of-way.
After stopping completely and looking both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when there is a safe gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: You must let traffic already in the roundabout go first. Enter only when you see a safe opening in traffic.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers of railroad crossings ahead. Drive with extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: If convicted of leaving the scene of a crash, your driver license can be revoked for up to:

options.text: Three months
Six months
Nine months
One year

questions.explanation: If you are convicted of leaving the scene of a crash, your license can be revoked for up to one year.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on your left at an unmarked intersection where you arrive at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to traffic when entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley. You must also yield to pedestrians on any crossing sidewalk.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks right away and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any train coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing railroad tracks. This is especially important when there are no lights or gates. Never cross until your whole vehicle fits on the other side. Do not change gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down to exit the interstate?

options.text: Halfway through the exit lane.
As you approach the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well ahead of time. Do not start to slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under bad conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones or work zones. If weather or road work makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: How should you always think of railroad crossings?

options.text: Safe to cross because a train is unlikely to be coming.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park a car.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.
